_readme: Freshness allowances for every series in site/mx/fiscal/data.js. One file feeds three readers: scripts/mx-fiscal/fetch.mjs
embeds it in data.js (MX_DATA.freshness), the page turns a block amber in the reader's browser when a series is older than
its allowance, and scripts/mx-fiscal/check-freshness.mjs fails the workflow and opens the mx-fiscal-health issue.
`bd` = Mexican business days after the observation date (daily series); `days` = calendar days after the END of the
stamped period (weekly, monthly, quarterly). An allowance is the publisher's normal lag plus a margin: past it, a newer
figure exists that the fetch has failed to pick up. `byFreq` applies unless the key has its own entry in `bySeries`.
Calibrated on 2026-10-01 against the observed lags in data.js.

D.why: Banxico SIE daily series (target rate, TIIE, FIX, UDI) carry the previous business day by the 19:30 UTC run

W.why: weekly balance sheet and reserves (Tuesday for the previous Friday), weekly Cetes auctions

M.why: SHCP monthly public finances: last business day of the following month (~30 days), plus a margin

Q.why: quarterly accounts: INEGI nominal GDP ~55 days after the quarter, the next one ~90 days later

vgTotal.why: Banxico publishes holdings of government securities with a lag of about 6 to 8 business days

cetes364.why: the 364-day Cetes are auctioned every other week

inpc.why: INEGI publishes the monthly INPC around the 9th of the following month

inflExp12m.why: Banxico publishes the monthly survey of forecasters on the first business days of the following month

vgPlazoPromedio.why: monthly, published early in the following month

deudaBrutaSPEA.why: quarterly, SHCP's quarterly report 30 days after the quarter, republished by Banxico
